I was bored and thinking about terrariums I've been seeing on youtube recently. I decided I want one so I put together the things needed on amazon to see what the cost would be. I could save a little money by using some things from nature outside, but I'm going for a tropical terrarium and we don't really have tropical plants other than ferns, and taking things from the environment is likely to grow random bacteria/fungus that'll kill everything in the terrarium. So I ordered a set of small tropical plants, a gallon glass jar with a wide mouth, some sterile soil mix, 2.5 pounds of activated charcoal, and some fresh live moss.

The general construction will be, from top to bottom:

Plants/insects, I'll go out in the woods and pick up some springtails and pillbugs, and maybe a small millipede or two if I see some. I might also grab a fern depending on which plants I end up getting, if I don't have enough appropriate plants (it's a random assortment I bought) to fill the terrarium.

Moss/soil for a base substrate

Activated charcoal to reduce acidity, contaminants, and smell

Moss to keep soil substrate/charcoal from working its way into the bottom layer

Pebbles in the very bottom to prevent dirty, stagnant muddy water. Anything that doesn't get absorbed by the plants will go to the bottom rather than rotting the roots of the plants. I have pebbles in the garden, I'll just wash them with some dish soap and clean water, no reason to pay for more for a small layer in the bottom of the jar right now.

Of course I'll update with pictures once I get everything together. A few of the things will probably take a week or more to arrive.
